I will put the full 19.1 mu into the same wheat-maize rotation again. That is how this land pays, and with only me at home I will not make the management too fancy. I have farmed here many years, so I start from what usually works in our area and then adjust a little for cost and yield. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, put the main fertilizer under before sowing, and keep three irrigations in mind: winter water if the field is dry, one at jointing, one around grain filling if needed. Wheat cannot be starved here, especially with well water available, so I will keep nitrogen around 14 kg per mu and match it with phosphorus and potassium instead of using only urea. For maize after wheat, I will save labor and time with no-tillage sowing into the stubble, use hybrid seed, give enough bottom fertilizer, then topdress once at the big flare stage. Around here, if maize loses fertilizer at that stage, the ears get short fast, so I would rather spend a bit more than lose yield. I will plan two irrigations for maize in a normal year, one after sowing if moisture is short and one around tasseling to filling. On sprays, I will keep wheat at three rounds and maize at two rounds, because disease, weeds, and insects all cost money if I let them get ahead. With this kind of management on 19.1 mu in Quzhou, I will aim for steady yield, not gamble on either cutting inputs too hard or chasing the highest possible number.
